sentences.text: The applicant is in judicial custody since 18.09.2016.
His first application has been dismissed in default vide order dated 03.11.2023, passed in M.Cr.C. No.35741/2023.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application, case diary and the relevant material on record.
Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant is in custody since 18.09.2016.
He has already undergone judicial custody for almost 09 years and 03 months.
The trial is not progressing at appropriate stage.
As per status report, 22 witnesses have been examined out of total 32 prosecution witnesses.
The case is pending for the receipt NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:268 2 MCRC-57612-2025 of case property.
The trial would take time to conclude.

sentences.text: Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant and his family members.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the trial.
Considering the long custody of the applicant, he may be extended benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel further refers to 08 criminal antecedents of the applicant, as mentioned in the case diary.

He further submits that in one matter registered vide Crime No.31/2017, the applicant has been convicted for offence punishable under Sections 420,
406, 409 and 34 of IPC.
In reply, learned counsel for the applicant submits that 07 matters are pending for trial against the applicant.

The order of sentence has been stayed by the Appellate Court vide order dated 10.11.2025,
passed in Cri.A. No.1567/2024.
Considered.

As per the accusation, the applicant - Poonamchand and his associates defrauded the investors on promise of handsome profit and induced them to invest in "Pragya Dairy and Agro Ltd.," and misappropriated the invested amount to the tune of Rs.86,75,110/-.
The applicant was arrested on 18.09.2016 for offence punishable under Sections 406, 409, 419, 420, 34 of IPC and under Section 6 of Madhya Pradesh Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam, 2000.

sentences.text: The material prosecution witnesses have been examined.
The trial would take time to conclude.
The veracity of prosecution and complicity of the applicant will be determined after evidence in the trial.
As informed, the applicant was aged around 53 years function at the time of arrest.
He was a Director of Private Investment Company and has the responsibility of dependent family.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:268 3 MCRC-57612-2025 no possibility of fleeing from justice.
Considering the socio-economic status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the remining witnesses by the applicant.
There appears to be no compelling reason to further continue long incarceration of the applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.
Considering the long custody as well as in the light of aforestated facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
